# import packages and functions
```{r import packages and functions}
suppressMessages(library(igraph))
suppressMessages(library(ggplot2))
suppressMessages(library(dplyr))
suppressMessages(library(RColorBrewer))

```

# load two networks first
```{r}
g1 <- readRDS('graph_shrinkage_res1.1_s0.15_TexTerm__subset_TFs_v2.rds')
g2 <- readRDS('graph_shrinkage_res1.1_s0.15_TRM__subset_TFs_v2.rds')
gv1 <- igraph::as_data_frame(g1, "vertices")
gv2 <- igraph::as_data_frame(g2, "vertices")

common_tfs <- intersect(gv1$name, gv2$name)
tex_tfs <- setdiff(gv1$name, gv2$name)
trm_tfs <- setdiff(gv2$name, gv1$name)

```

# combine two networks
Prepare the edge info
```{r}
# extract edge info: take mean if edge exists in both networks
ge1 <- igraph::as_data_frame(g1) %>% select(from, to, corr) %>% transform(from=pmin(from, to), to=pmax(from,to))
ge2 <- igraph::as_data_frame(g2) %>% select(from, to, corr) %>% transform(from=pmin(from, to), to=pmax(from,to))
ge <- ge1 %>% full_join(ge2, by = c('from','to')) %>% 
    mutate(corr=ifelse(is.na(corr.x), corr.y, ifelse(is.na(corr.y), corr.x, (corr.x+corr.y)/2)),
           edge.color=ifelse(is.na(corr.x), '#009051', ifelse(is.na(corr.y), '#8AAA75', '#808080')),
           type=ifelse(is.na(corr.x), 'trm', ifelse(is.na(corr.y), 'tex', 'common'))) |> 
        select(from,to,corr,edge.color,type) |> na.omit()
print(knitr::kable(head(ge), caption = 'edge meta') |> kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = 'scale_down'))
print(dim(ge))

```

# ==============================================================================
# PART 2: Load OLD Implementation Results for Comparison
# ==============================================================================

```{r}
old_tex_file <- "graph_shrinkage_res0.9_s0.15_TexTerm__subset_TFs_v2.rds"
old_trm_file <- "graph_shrinkage_res0.9_s0.15_TRM__subset_TFs_v2.rds"

# Function to read old CSVs and standardize edge direction (from < to)
process_old_edges <- function(filepath) {
  g1 <- readRDS(filepath)
  gv1 <- igraph::as_data_frame(g1, "vertices")
  ge1 <- igraph::as_data_frame(g1) %>% select(from, to, corr) %>% transform(from=pmin(from, to), to=pmax(from,to))
  return(ge1)
}

# Load and process
df_old_tex <- process_old_edges(old_tex_file)
df_old_trm <- process_old_edges(old_trm_file)

# Combine Old Tex and TRM to define specificity types
ge_old <- df_old_tex %>% full_join(df_old_trm, by = c('from','to')) %>% 
    mutate(corr=ifelse(is.na(corr.x), corr.y, ifelse(is.na(corr.y), corr.x, (corr.x+corr.y)/2)),
           edge.color=ifelse(is.na(corr.x), '#009051', ifelse(is.na(corr.y), '#8AAA75', '#808080')),
           type=ifelse(is.na(corr.x), 'trm', ifelse(is.na(corr.y), 'tex', 'common'))) |> 
        select(from,to,corr,edge.color,type) |> na.omit()
print(knitr::kable(head(ge_old), caption = 'edge meta') |> kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = 'scale_down'))
print(dim(ge_old))

```

# ==============================================================================
# PART 3: Compare Edge Specificity (New vs Old)
# ==============================================================================
```{r}
# 1. Merge the two dataframes to align edges
# We use full_join because some edges might exist in Old but dropped in New (or vice versa)
edge_comparison <- full_join(
  ge %>% select(from, to, type) %>% rename(type_new = type),
  ge_old %>% select(from, to, type) %>% rename(type_old = type),
  by = c("from", "to")
)

# 2. Handle missing edges (Edges present in one but not the other)
# Replace NA with "Absent" to track dropped/gained edges explicitly
edge_comparison <- edge_comparison %>%
  mutate(
    type_new = ifelse(is.na(type_new), "Absent", type_new),
    type_old = ifelse(is.na(type_old), "Absent", type_old)
  )

# 3. Calculate Confusion Matrix Stats
confusion_stats <- edge_comparison %>%
  count(type_old, type_new) %>%
  group_by(type_old) %>%
  mutate(
    total_in_old_category = sum(n),
    percent = (n / total_in_old_category) * 100
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Print quantitative check for Tex-specific robustness
tex_conservation <- confusion_stats %>% 
  filter(type_old == "tex", type_new == "tex") %>% 
  pull(percent)

print(paste0("Robustness of Tex-specific edges: ", round(tex_conservation, 1), "% of edges identified as Tex-specific in the old method are still Tex-specific in the new method."))


# 4. Visualization: Confusion Heatmap
# Logic: X-axis is the "Old Truth" (Previous Method), Y-axis is the "New Outcome".
# The diagonal represents conserved specificity.

# Define custom order for axes for clarity
type_levels <- c("tex", "trm", "common", "Absent")

p_robustness <- ggplot(confusion_stats, aes(x = factor(type_old, levels = type_levels), 
                                            y = factor(type_new, levels = type_levels), 
                                            fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), color = "black", size = 3.5, vjust = -0.5) + # Raw Count
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0("(", round(percent, 1), "%)")), 
            color = "black", size = 2.5, vjust = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) + # Percentage
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F0F0F0", high = "#4E79A7", trans = "log1p") + # Log scale helps visualize large differences
  labs(
    title = "Robustness of Edge Specificity (Old vs. New Implementation)",
    subtitle = "Percentage indicates how 'Old' edges were reclassified in the 'New' method",
    x = "Edge Type (Old Method)",
    y = "Edge Type (New Method)",
    fill = "# Edges"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

print(p_robustness)

# 5. Optional: Save the discrepancies for inspection
# If you want to check which Tex edges were lost
lost_tex_edges <- edge_comparison %>%
  filter(type_old == "tex", type_new == "Absent")

head(lost_tex_edges)
```
